Aug 2025 meeting: written contracts, bank-paid salaries, RSSB, medical insurance, working-hour limits, vetted guards, penalties warned. About 15 licensed companies and 75+ security cooperatives. coverage.found: 0.2% of customs value, collected at border via RRA, from 1 Jul 2025; no importer-side filing seen. Folded into C-RW-09.

coverage.found: ECD under Ministry of Gender and Family Promotion; centres accredited by districts or RDB; harmonised ECD standards in development (Jan 2026 conference). No licensing register or periodic filing found. Nothing new; group A category 20 overlap.

coverage.found: CMA licenses warehouse receipt operators; implementation status unconfirmed; EAX operates first system since 2014. Few operators, so buyer pool is small. Folded into C-RW-07.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: The duty sits with RICA (Rwanda Inspectorate, Competition and Consumer Protection Authority), via Irembo, under the 2012 agrochemicals law and its orders. Dealers (importers, distributors, retailers, fumigators) need three things. First, a premises registration (14 days; setbacks of 50 m from schools, health facilities and water, 20 m from food manufacturing, no residential use). Second, a dealer operating licence (5 days; needs a notarized diploma and contract for qualified personnel, a labelled carrier vehicle, and an RDB certificate). Third, for fumigators, a fumigation operating licence (14 days, reportedly 50,000 Rwf; needs records of agrochemicals used and fumigation certificates issued). Inspectors do routine inspections. Penalty for banned agrochemicals: up to 3 years' prison and up to Rwf 5m fine (undated Umunota report). Product registration (pesticides, fertiliser, biopesticides) is separate and is done by manufacturers/importers with trials, so it is out of scope. Licence validity (reported as 5 years, renewable, from an undated New Times piece) and renewal fees are unconfirmed. Subsidised-fertiliser agro-dealers (about 1,046 registered in 2019) transact through the government-run Smart Nkunganire System (BK TecHouse with RAB), which covers ordering, farmer registration and stock management. That overlaps K04 and K09's state-system problem. No 2025-2026 rule change, crackdown or dealer-software product was found. Nothing new beyond K04, except the fumigator niche (see ledger).

result.competitor: The state portal iRIMS handles applications and payments only. I found no commercial software and no named Rwandan consultancy offering dossier, SOP, GMP or CAPA preparation in 2 English-language searches. Rwanda FDA's own support is workshops run with donors (USDA TRASE / Land O'Lakes Venture 37, plus the Private Sector Federation, 2022). I didn't run a Kinyarwanda or French search, so informal consultants can't be ruled out.
result.duty: Rwanda FDA food premises licence for manufacturers (Guideline DIS/GDL/005, effective 20/02/2022, revision added sanctions and fines; Regulation FD/FSMIL/TRG/007 Rev_1 on operational licences, adopted 21/10/2024). GMP Regulations for food manufacturers FDISM/FDIC/TRG/008 Rev_0, in force 30/12/2022. Regulations on inspections of processed food dated 23/10/2024. Product registration for low-risk domestic foods (flours, honey, beverages, confectionery, bakery) needs the premises licence, a mandatory GMP inspection application through iRIMS, payment through iRIMS and 3 packaged samples. High-risk foods also need a GMP certificate and a stability study on 3 batches. The New Times (2022) calls premises licensing annual, at about Rwf200,000 per component. Unverified: the exact validity term in the 2024 regulation, the fine amounts, and any micro-enterprise exemption. The application form does have an SME manufacturer category.
result.market: Rwanda FDA mapped 813 agro-processing factories in 2019 to May 2020. Of these, 514 had applied for a premises licence and 155 were licensed (New Times, Feb 2022). NAEB counts 258 horticulture processors, 57% of them cooperatives. Rwanda FDA publishes licensee lists (food manufacturers with an FBO licence, June 2026; with a premises licence, March 2026), but those PDFs returned 404, so I have no current count. A rough estimate is under 1,000 formal small processors.
result.reason: The duty is real. Rwanda FDA requires a food premises licence (DIS/GDL/005, effective 20/02/2022; operational-licence regulation FD/FSMIL/TRG/007 Rev_1, adopted 21/10/2024) and GMP rules (in force 30/12/2022). Low-risk products also need registration through iRIMS, a GMP inspection and 3 samples. The premises licence is annual, per a 2022 New Times report. Fees are about Rwf200k per component, and owners already call that too high for small firms. I found no software or consultancy for the dossier, SOP or CAPA work, but my competitor search was in English only. The market is small: 813 agro-processing factories were mapped in 2020, and only 155 were licensed. I couldn't reach the current Rwanda FDA licensee lists (404). Fines and validity terms are unverified. A small market with low ability to pay means a low score.

result.competitor: No Rwanda-specific guard-firm compliance or roster product was found. Generic tools already cover the payroll/RSSB core: the Odoo l10n_rw_payroll module, Workpay, Mercans managed payroll, and EOR firms (Ontop, Playroll). FaidiHR publishes Rwanda payroll guides, but I did not confirm it sells a product. The state's MyRRA e-tax portal (unified PAYE/RSSB declaration) is free. None of these covers vetting or training certificates, guard deployment or hours, or an RNP inspection file.
result.duty: Duties have been in force since the September 2020 private security law, with compliance due after a 2-year grace period. The RNP ISPSP department licenses firms after a joint vetting committee review. Guards are vetted and must complete at least 3 months of training at a police-approved centre. Inspections are ongoing, and penalties are suspension, licence withdrawal or prosecution. Labour duties were restated at the 28 Aug 2025 MIFOTRA/RNP meeting: written contracts, wages paid through banks, RSSB, medical insurance, limits on hours, vetted guards, and regular self-evaluation. Officials warned of penalties but named no specific fines. The monthly PAYE+RSSB declaration to RRA is due by the 15th; vendor pages say late-filing penalties are 20-60%. I found no statutory periodic report to RNP or guard-register form (not verified).
result.market: The RNP article reports 15 licensed private security companies and over 75 active cooperatives. Guard numbers are about 30,000 (2024 inspection) or 23,000+ across 16 firms (around 2022). That makes about 90 buyers at most, concentrated in a few large firms.
result.reason: The duties are real. A September 2020 private security law gave firms a 2-year grace period to comply. Under it, RNP vets and licenses firms, requires 3 months of training for guards, and inspects. Penalties are suspension, licence withdrawal or prosecution. At the August 2025 MIFOTRA/RNP meeting, firms were told to use written contracts, pay wages through banks, pay RSSB and medical insurance, and limit hours, with penalties threatened. I found no RNP periodic report or statutory guard register. No guard-specific Rwandan tool turned up, but the core payroll/RSSB job is already sold: Odoo l10n_rw_payroll, Workpay, Mercans, FaidiHR (not confirmed as a product). Monthly PAYE/RSSB filing on MyRRA is free. The market is tiny: 15 licensed companies and 75+ cooperatives. The cooperatives likely pay little.

Duty is real: BNR Regulation 89/2025 (gazetted 30 May 2025, in force on publication) bans pricing, quoting or invoicing in foreign currency without BNR authorisation. Fines are RWF 5-10m, or 50-100% of the transaction. Forex bureaus also report through a shared association system (RFBAIS, 2018) and BNR electronic data templates. I found no software for the core job. But for most businesses the duty is simply "don't quote in dollars", so there is no recurring workflow to automate. Bureaus are few and already served by the association system. Authorised receivers are a niche whose criteria I could not read. I did not read the gazetted text. Low pain, frequency and willingness to pay, so I score 3.

Duty is likely real. RURA Regulation 009/R/SAN-EWS/RURA/2023 (12 May 2023) sets a licensing regime and requires regular reporting and inspections. A 2016 liquid waste collection regulation (005/R/SAN-EWS/RURA/2016) also exists. The FAOLEX status is ambiguous: one search said "Repealed" and another said not repealed. I could not open the full text, so penalties, reporting frequency and licence categories are unconfirmed. I found no count of licensed haulers and no competing software, though the search was shallow. The buyer base looks tiny, probably dozens of operators. RURA also plans to move desludging to WASAC with sanitation fees on water bills, which could remove the buyer. Willingness to pay is likely low, so I score it 2.

The duty looks real. Law N° 058/2024, in force 19 July 2024 per PwC, requires NGOs to file annual reports, declare bank accounts, and keep admin costs to 20% (Article 9). The AllAfrica report gives a 18 July 2026 compliance deadline, which has passed, and I found no extension. I could not read the law text. It is not clear how often NGOs file, what the penalty is for each duty, or how many NGOs are registered, so I have no market count. The RGB notice I fetched covers faith-based organisations, not NGOs, and cites no law number. I found no dedicated NGO compliance software or RGB filing portal, but the search was thin. Weak points: the deadline has passed, buyers are small donor-funded NGOs that may already report to donors, and willingness to pay is low.
